16 A bungee jumper jumps from a platform and is decelerated by an elastic bungee cord, as shown.

When the jumper makes the jump, his initial gravitational potential energy is converted into his
kinetic energy and into elastic potential energy in the cord.
At which part of the jump are all three types of energy non-zero?
A
on the platform before the jump
B
on the way down before the cord has started to extend
C
on the way down as he decelerates
D
at the bottom of the jump when he is stationary

hints: Check height above the ground for gravitational potential energy $mgh$ - the jumper is above the ground in every option except the reference level, so focus on the other two energies.
Recall elastic potential energy $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ needs extension $x$ of the bungee cord, so it is zero on the platform and during free fall before the cord tightens.
Recall kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ needs speed $v$, so compare falling while still moving with being stationary at the bottom to leave only the stage with motion plus stretch.
walkthrough: State the test for each energy to be non-zero: gravitational potential energy needs height above the ground, kinetic energy needs non-zero speed, elastic potential energy needs extension of the bungee cord.
On the platform before the jump the jumper has height but speed $v = 0$ and cord extension $x = 0$, so only gravitational potential energy is non-zero.
On the way down before the cord extends the jumper has height and speed, but $x = 0$, so gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy are non-zero while elastic potential energy is zero.
On the way down as he decelerates the cord has extended so $x > 0$, he is still above the ground and still moving, so height, speed and extension are all present.

At the bottom when stationary, speed $v = 0$ so kinetic energy is zero, even though height and cord extension give the other two energies. This leaves only the decelerating fall with all three non-zero. This is option C.

A.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is non-zero on the platform, but kinetic energy is zero because speed is zero and elastic potential energy is zero because the cord is unstretched.

B.explanation: The jumper is falling so gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy are non-zero, but elastic potential energy is zero because the cord has not started to extend.

C.explanation: The jumper is still above the ground and still moving while the cord is stretched, so gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy and elastic potential energy are all non-zero.

D.explanation: At the instant he is stationary kinetic energy is zero, even though gravitational potential energy and elastic potential energy in the stretched cord are non-zero.
